frequency_question: What proportion of privileged or expedited congressional disapproval resolutions successfully complete all necessary legislative steps (both chambers passing the measure and surviving or overriding a veto) within their statutory time limits?
membership_rule: Includes all joint resolutions of disapproval introduced under statutory frameworks (such as the Atomic Energy Act or Arms Export Control Act) where a specific fast-track clock applies. Excludes ordinary bills that lack expedited floor scheduling privileges.

cases.name: 2017 Iran Sanctions / Review Act related measures

coverage_note: 5 major historical fast-track foreign policy/arms control disapproval fights examined; roughly 8-10 total exist across modern history.
known_gaps: Minor procedural variations across different specific statutes (AEF vs AECA vs INA) alter exact floor time guarantees slightly, but overall structural timeline constraints remain similar.
skeleton: Total statutory disapproval resolutions introduced under fast-track mechanisms in modern legislative history, tracked against completion of all passage and veto-override milestones.
multiplier: 5 instances evaluated against fast-track completion criteria yielding successful passage and enactment over veto once
validity_reason: Statutory fast-track mechanisms (like AECA Section 123 provisions) remain stable unless Congress alters the underlying statutes governing nuclear cooperation review.
